images.filename: Broad Plateau west of Craig Eigiau - geograph.org.uk - 107442.jpg
images.caption: Broad Plateau west of Craig Eigiau. The foreground shows a faint track developing as an easy route between Cwm Eigiau and the ridge between Foel Grach and Carnedd Llewellyn. This sector also contains Melynllyn Reservoir, a few hundred feet lower and out of sight to the right of this view. The central top is Carnedd Llewellyn which is the 2nd highest peak in Snowdonia at 3,484 feet.

images.filename: Carnedd Llewelyn from below Foel Grach - geograph.org.uk - 107454.jpg
images.caption: Carnedd Llewelyn from below Foel Grach. Carnedd Llewelyn is the 2nd highest peak in Snowdonia at 3,484 feet and on this particular day was covered in a thin layer of snow and a thick layer of frost. The temperature was around -8 degrees C and the wind was blowing from the east making it a particularly cold day. Perfect conditions for winter walking.Some faint figures can be seen descending from the summit.
images.alt: Carnedd Llewelyn from below Foel Grach. images.filename: Awyrlun o Gastell y Bere yn Hydref 2024 - Aerial image of Welsh castle Castell y Bere near Tywyn, Gwynedd, Wales 50.png
images.caption:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
Castell y Bere is a Welsh castle in south Gwynedd, Wales. It was one of the most important castles of the princes of Gwynedd in the 13th century. It was built by Llywelyn the Great to keep out the invading English. It is believed that the poet Gruffudd ab yr Ynad Goch composed his famous elegy for Prince Llywelyn ap Gruffudd (Llywelyn II) in Castell y Bere in December 1282 or early 1283.
images.alt:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.

images.caption:
Blaenau Ffestiniog railway station - On the left of the picture, Arriva Trains Wales British Rail Class 153 DMU 153327 stands at the standard gauge platform for a Conwy Valley Line service. While on the right of the picture the narrow gauge Ffestiniog Railway locomotive Linda is about to run-round the train in preparation for the journey to Porthmadog.

Note also the different platform heights for the different gauges.
